questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common disease associated with S. agalactiae?
questions.solutionHtml:
Neonatal sepsis
  • Group B Streptococcus (S agalactiae) is the most common cause of neonatal meningitis.
  • Approximately 5–40% of women are vaginal or rectal carriers of group B Streptococcus (GBS). Hence, the GBS infection is common in neonates and in pregnancy.


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 284, 437., Essentials Of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 525-26.

questions.stem: Read the following 2 statements and answer:Faucial diphtheria can cause death due to myocarditis.Bacteraemia is seen in diphtheria.Select the correct answer from the given below code:

options.label: A
options.text: Statement 1 and Statement 2 is true, and Statement 2 is the correct explanation of Statement 1

options.label: B
options.text: Statement 1 and Statement 2 are true, but Statement 2 is not the correct explanation of Statement 1

options.label: C
options.text: Statement 1 is true and statement 2 is false

questions.answerText: Statement 1 is true and statement 2 is false
questions.solutionHtml:
Statement 1 is true and statement 2 is false
  • Pathogenesis of diphtheria is toxin mediated. Diphtheria is a toxemia but never a bacteremia.
  • Bacilli are noninvasive, present only at local sites (pharynx), secrete the toxin which spreads via bloodstream to various organs.
  • Faucial diphtheria: Diphtheria toxin elicits an inflammatory response, that leads to necrosis of the epithelium and exudate formation This leads to formation of mucosal ulcers, lined by a tough leathery greyish white pseudomembrane coat; composed of an inner band of fibrin surrounded by neutrophils, RBCs and bacteria.
  • Extension of pseudomembrane: In severe cases, it may extend into the larynx and bronchial airways, which may result in fatal airway obstruction leading to asphyxia. This mandates immediate tracheostomy.
  • Polyneuropathy and myocarditis are the late toxic manifestations of diphtheria, occurring after weeks of infection.


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 361-64., Essentials Of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 621-22.

questions.stem: A construction worker presents with a lock jaw and muscle rigidity. He has a history of exposure to a rusted iron nail through an existing wound. Which of the following is the mechanism of action of the toxin responsible for this presentation?

options.label: B
options.text: Inhibition of glycine and GABA release

questions.answerText: Inhibition of glycine and GABA release
questions.solutionHtml:
Inhibition of glycine and GABA release

The Given clinical picture is s/o Tetanus.

  • Tetanus bacilli enter through: Injury (superficial abrasions, Punctured wounds, road traffic accidents)
  • Surgery done without proper asepsis
  • Neonates: Following abortion/delivery, due to unhygienic practices
  • Otitis media (otogenic tetanus)


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 438-441,Essentials Of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 702-4.

options.label: B

Essentials Of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 627-30.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old female comes to the OPD with dysuria. She has non-irritant profuse white discharge from her vagina. On examination her labia were inflamed and swollen. The openings of her urethra and Bartholin's glands were congested. On collection of her endocervical discharge, intracellular gram- negative diplococci were found. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Neisseria gonorrhoeae
  • Gonococcus is a very important cause of urethritis. In this case microscopic examination of urethral discharge shows intracellular gram negative diplococci which confirms the causative organism as N gonorrhoeae.


Essentials Of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 764-766.

questions.stem: Which of the following immunodeficiency diseases predisposes to infection by catalase positive organisms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Chronic granulomatous disease
  • Chronic granulomatous disease (CGD) is an immunodeficiency disorder that occurs due to defect in NADPH oxidase.
  • It is associated with recurrent infections mainly with catalase positive organisms.


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 254-260,Essentials Of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition. Page No. 208-212

questions.stem: Out of the given lab techniques, which of the following can be used for a sterilization of disposable pipette tip?AutoclaveHot air ovenMicrowavingEthyl alcohol 70%Select the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1 only
  • Disposable pipette tips are sterilized by autoclaving and cold sterilization methods as these cannot withstand the high temperature of a hot air oven. Due to the possibility of uneven energy distribution, which can lead to uneven sterilization, microwaving is less suitable for sterilization.
  • Heat labile, cannot be sterilized by dry heat sterilization based methods.
  • Glassware, wax, oils, powders and all metallic instruments are sterilized in a hot air oven.
  • 70% Ethyl alcohol is not sporicidal and hence cannot be used for sterilization.


Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 124-5.Essentials Of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 253-8.

questions.stemHtml: Negative staining of CSF mount of an HIV patient is shown in the figure. Which of the following is true with respect to the organism shown in the figure?

options.label: A
options.text: Lung is the primary site of infection

options.label: B
options.text: Associated with budding yeast cells and pseudo hyphae

options.label: D
options.text: Opportunistic infections are seen in patients with CD4 count 900

questions.answerText: Lung is the primary site of infection
questions.solutionHtml:
Lung is the primary site of infection
  • Cryptococcal infection is acquired by inhalation of aerosolized forms of Cryptococcus.
  • Both yeast cells as well as basidiospores (the sexual stage of Cryptococcus) are infectious.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 687,Essentials Of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 739-41.

questions.stemHtml: A 50-year-old patient who underwent a renal transplant recently, came with complaints of watery diarrhoea. Stool sample revealed oocysts of size 30 x 15 microns (shown in the image). Identify the organism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cystoisospora belli
  • Patients who had recent renal transplant must be immunocompromised, now presenting with diarrhea and stool examination showing acid fast oocysts with size of 30X 15 microns s/o Cystoisospora  belli species of coccidian parasites.


Essentials Of Medical Parasitology, Apurba S Sastry, 2nd Edition, Page No. 38-41, 100-107.

questions.stem: Which of the following parasites reproduce directly from egg to larva without fertilisation through parthenogenesis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Strongyloides stercoralis
  • Strongyloides stercoralis is an ovoviviparous organism, larvae immediately hatches out from eggs, therefore stool examination reveals larvae (rhabditiform).
  • The adult females directly lay eggs without fertilization, k/a Parthenogenesis.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th Edition, Lange Mcgraw Hill Publications, Page No. 747,Ananthanarayan And Paniker's Textbook Of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 594,Essentials Of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 457-68

questions.stem: Read the following 2 statements and answer: Assertion: Late trophozoite and schizont stage in Plasmodium falciparum are not seen in blood smears.Reason: The RBC shows cytoadherence to the endothelial cells of the internal organs.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is true.

questions.answerText: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
questions.solutionHtml:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
  • falciparum infection is distinguished by the appearance of only ring forms of early trophozoites and banana gametocytes, both of which can be found in the peripheral blood, Schizonts are not seen in the peripheral smear due to their sequestration.
  • In P falciparum infection, since the parasites are sequestrated back in deep vessels, they can avoid frequent spleen passage, hence can escape splenic clearance and also their detection in PBS examination unless there is very high level of parasitemia.
  • The size of the RBC is usually normal. Double dots in the rings are common.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page Number: 724-25, 735-36,Essentials Of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 346-51. Ananthanarayan And Paniker's Textbook Of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page Number: 321-4.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a clinical manifestation of Parvovirus B19 infection?

options.label: C
options.text: Transient aplastic crisis in children with haemolytic anaemia

options.label: D
options.text: Persistent anaemia or Pure red cell aplasia in immunodeficient individuals

questions.solutionHtml:
Febrile illness with petechial rash
  • Parvovirus B 19 are responsible for a common childhood exanthema called as erythema infectiosum in humans which can present as a febrile illness with exanthematous rash not petechial rash.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th Edition, Lange Mcgraw Hill Publications, Page No. 780,Ananthanarayan And Paniker Textbook Of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 589,Essentials Of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 556-7

questions.stem: An 18-day-old baby presents with altered sensorium, neck rigidity with vesicular lesions on the anterior abdomen and the forearm. The mother revealed a history of treatment for painful genital ulcers in the genital region 1 year ago and the baby was born through vaginal delivery. Scrapings from the lesions reveals multinucleated giant cells. Which of the following is the most likely involved organism?
questions.solutionHtml:
HSV-2
  • Herpes simplex virus (HSV- 2) commonly causes encephalitis and can also cause meningitis.  Herpes simplex viruses (HSV) are the second most common cause of viral meningitis, next to enteroviruses; accounting for 5% of cases. Scrapings from the lesions in the mother revealing multinucleated giant cells is s/o HSV-2 infection.
  • History of genital herpes is an important clue that HSV-2 meningitis can occur in babies of women.


Ananthanarayan And Paniker Textbook Of Microbiology, 11th Edition, Page No. 472,Essentials Of Medical Microbiology, Apurba S Sastry, 3rd Edition, Page No. 708-16, 797-8
